title: India gold market update: Seasonal demand shows early strength
gist: Indian gold demand is picking up into the festive and wedding season after September's 8.5% price drop: the domestic discount narrowed to US$8/oz, ETF inflows hit a seven-month high and listed jewellers grew revenue 20-30% y/y. Official imports collapsed 81% y/y as recycled old gold and other domestic supply replaced them, while a SEBI-linked suspension of fresh gold FoF subscriptions aims to curb imports but is expected to have limited impact on flows.

themes.theme: Gold price pullback and Indian domestic discount

insights.claim: Gold ended September 2026 at US$4,176/oz, down 8.5% m/m, as higher US Treasury yields, a stronger dollar and reduced futures positioning outweighed strong global ETF inflows.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Rates and dollar dominated gold's September drop even against ETF buying, so macro drivers still set the price.
insights.quote: higher US Treasury yields, a stronger dollar and reduced futures positioning weighed on prices

insights.claim: Indian domestic gold prices fell only 4.8% in September to INR147,613/10g because rupee weakness cushioned the international decline; in October domestic prices slipped about 1% as the INR gained while international prices held flat.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: For Indian holders, currency moves materially dampen or amplify global gold moves.
insights.quote: weakness in the INR cushioning some of the decline in international prices

insights.claim: India's domestic gold discount narrowed from an average US$66/oz in September to US$8/oz by 16 October 2026, reflecting improving seasonal demand.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A shrinking discount shows physical demand in India is firming, which supports the price.
insights.quote: from an average of US$66/oz in September to US$8/oz as of 16 October
insights.locator: Domestic gold price discounts have narrowed

insights.claim: The persistent discount to import parity signals adequate domestic gold supply in India, with industry citing old-gold supply and unofficial inflows as contributors.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Recycled gold and unofficial flows are standing in for official imports, so import data understates real demand.
insights.quote: industry feedback citing old-gold supply and unofficial inflows as contributing factors
insights.locator: Domestic gold price discounts have narrowed

themes.theme: Festive and wedding season jewellery demand

insights.claim: Indian seasonal gold demand is gaining traction going into the festive and wedding period, helped by the recent price decline, with manufacturers reporting healthy order flows as retailers restock and footfall improving.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Near-term Indian physical demand looks set to provide support on price dips.
insights.quote: Manufacturers are reporting healthy order flows as retailers replenish inventories

insights.claim: Lower prices support jewellery spending in India, but elevated price levels may continue to limit volume growth in the festive and wedding season.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Expect value growth rather than tonnage growth from Indian jewellery demand.
insights.quote: elevated price levels may continue to limit volume growth

insights.claim: Indian bar and coin demand has reportedly moderated as gold's price momentum eased, cooling some of the investment buying seen during the earlier rally.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Indian retail investment demand follows momentum, so it may lag while prices are rangebound.
insights.quote: Bar and coin demand, meanwhile, has reportedly moderated as price momentum has eased

themes.theme: Listed Indian jewellers: value over volume

insights.claim: Listed Indian jewellery retailers (Titan, Kalyan, PC Jewellers, P N Gadgil, Senco Gold) posted 20-30% y/y revenue growth in Jul-Sep 2026, even though key festivals moved into the Oct-Dec quarter this year.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Strong results without festival timing help point to a solid Oct-Dec quarter for Indian jewellery stocks.
insights.quote: strong double-digit revenue growth in the range of 20-30% y/y in the Jul-Sep quarter
insights.locator: Strong revenue growth for listed jewellers

insights.claim: Jeweller growth came from both same-store sales growth of around 20% and network expansion, with the largest players adding 42 stores during the quarter.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Organic same-store growth makes the earnings momentum look less dependent on store openings.
insights.quote: Same-store sales growth of around 20% suggests that growth was not only driven by the opening of new retail outlets
insights.locator: Growth was driven by a combination

insights.claim: Value growth is outpacing volume at Indian jewellers: buyer growth stayed in the mid-single digits while average ticket sizes rose by double digits on higher gold prices and premiumisation.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Revenue growth is mostly price-driven, not more tonnage or many more customers.
insights.quote: Buyer growth remained in the mid-single digits, while average ticket sizes increased by double digits

insights.claim: Old-gold exchange transactions at Indian jewellers rose more than 10% y/y and made up over 50% of sales for some retailers, which also feeds domestic gold supply.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Recycling is cutting into India's need for new imports, which weighs on official import demand.
insights.quote: rising by more than 10% y/y and accounting for over 50% of sales for some retailers

insights.claim: Indian jeweller management commentary is positive for the next two quarters, helped by festive demand, the peak wedding season, new stores and marketing campaigns; retailers are also tightening inventory to manage working-capital pressure from high gold prices.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Positive guidance plus inventory discipline supports the near-term outlook for the sector.
insights.quote: Management commentary is positive for the coming two quarters

themes.theme: Indian gold ETF flows on the dip

insights.claim: Indian gold ETF net inflows rose to INR44.5bn (US$466.2mn) in September 2026, a seven-month high; nearly 3t was added, taking holdings to 124t.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Indian investors bought the price dip, which signals sticky strategic demand.
insights.quote: net inflows rose to INR44.5bn (US$466.2mn), the highest in seven months

insights.claim: Inflows into Indian gold ETFs continued in early October, with an estimated INR17.22bn (US$181mn), or about 1.2t, in the first half of the month.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Investment demand has held up beyond a one-month reaction.

insights.claim: Indian gold ETF AUM fell 2.5% m/m to INR1,863bn (US$19.5bn) despite the inflows, because domestic gold prices fell 7%; gold ETFs were 2.25% of total mutual fund AUM, against 2.27% in January 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold's share of Indian fund portfolios is still small, leaving room for allocations to grow.
insights.quote: Gold ETFs accounted for 2.25% of overall mutual fund AUM

insights.claim: Indian gold ETFs added 140,231 new folios in September, up from around 4,000 in August, taking the total to 12.68mn, which suggests the price pullback drew in a wider group of investors.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A jump in new accounts points to a broadening retail base, not just existing holders adding.
insights.quote: Gold ETFs added 140,231 new folios (accounts) during September, a marked increase from around 4,000 in August

themes.theme: Regulatory curbs on gold Fund of Funds

insights.claim: From 16 October 2026, Indian mutual funds suspended fresh subscriptions into gold Fund of Funds, reportedly after talks with SEBI and probably to reduce gold imports; existing SIPs and redemptions are exempt. This follows the June limits on large direct subscriptions.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Indian authorities are moving step by step to curb investment-driven gold imports, a policy risk to Indian investment demand.
insights.quote: is likely aimed at lowering gold imports

insights.claim: Indian gold ETF demand totalled 29t in Jan-Sep 2026, around 7% of gold imports, up from about 5% a year earlier, which helps explain why policymakers are targeting the channel.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: ETFs' rising share of imports makes them a policy target at times of current-account pressure.
insights.quote: ETF demand totalled 29t, equivalent to around 7% of gold imports, compared with about 5% a year earlier
insights.locator: Gold ETFs have seen sustained inflows

insights.claim: Gold FoFs held INR633bn (US$6.63bn) at end-September, about one-third of total Indian gold ETF AUM (around 20% for some of the largest ETFs). The WGC still expects the suspension's impact on flows to be limited, because direct ETF investment and existing FoF SIPs continue and AUM share does not equal share of inflows.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The headline curb looks worse than it is, so don't overreact to Indian ETF flow risk.
insights.quote: The overall impact may thus be relatively contained

themes.theme: Digital gold, futures and collapsing imports

insights.claim: Indian digital gold purchases reached INR25.9bn (US$271mn) in September, up 83% y/y; volumes were 1.7t, and year-to-date purchases of 16.3t were 76% above 2025's 9.2t.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A fast-growing, low-ticket retail channel is widening the Indian gold investor base.
insights.quote: On a y-t-d basis, purchases totalled 16.3t compared with 9.2t in the corresponding period of 2025

insights.claim: Gold futures trading on MCX moderated in September, with average daily volume down 4% m/m to 18.3t and turnover down 10% to INR265bn (US$2.8bn), but both stayed about 20% above April-August averages.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Hedging and tactical positioning in India are still elevated, so speculative interest has not left.
insights.quote: both volumes and turnover approximately 20% above the April-August averages

insights.claim: India's September gold imports fell to US$1.8bn, the lowest since March 2024 and down 81% y/y, on gross volumes of about 20t; gold's share of merchandise imports dropped to 2.4% from 14%, likely because of more domestic supply, including recycled gold.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Weak official imports reflect a shift in supply, not weak demand, so don't read the import collapse as a bearish demand signal.
insights.quote: Gold imports fell sharply in September to US$1.8bn, the lowest level since March 2024
